00:00:03 Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, i'm Samir from Redwood inference, gonna run through agenda quick and then hand off to Lena for the deep runtime bits.
00:00:11 Priya (CTO): thanks, Samir. high level we need low p95 tail latency for patient-chart queries but must keep everything inside our VPC for compliance. we're evaluating private deployment.
00:00:23 Miguel (Lead SRE): quick note — we have strict egress through NAT GW and an outbound proxy, and DNS is internal resolver only, so anything that tries to call out will be blocked.
00:00:36 Lena (Redwood SE): okay perfect, that's useful context. agenda: network patterns (private link vs peering), egress strategies (nat vs proxy), dns/resolver behavior with KV cache, batching + cache hit patterns, and quantization/throughput tuning. i'll call out where the runtime expects ephemeral outbound.
00:00:55 Hannah (Security): also SOC2/ISO requirements — do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logs?
00:01:02 Samir (Redwood AE): yes, we support KMS integrations, can hand over the whitepaper. we do audit logging and SSO/SAML for console. we'll include the SOC2 attestation pdf.
00:01:12 Rajesh (MLOps): curious about KV cache — since we have lots of patient context prefixes, how do you avoid cache explosion and cross-tenant leakage?
00:01:22 Lena: good q. two levers: logical scoping and sharding. by default we partition KV by customer namespace + model+deployment id. TTLs are per-namespace; for patient-sensitive data we recommend short TTLs (30s-2m) and per-request encryption at rest. partitioning avoids cross-tenant keys in a worker shard.
00:01:44 Miguel: on the network side, our NAT sits in a dedicated egress subnet, and we see high conntrack counts when bursts hit. will your runtime open a ton of outbound connections?
00:01:55 Jordan (Solutions Eng): the runtime keeps persistent connections to internal services only — e.g., to a private metrics sink or KMS endpoint. token refreshes and healthchecks are small. most traffic is intra-node for KV cache and batching; we don't hit external endpoints per token generation.
00:02:12 Priya: what about PrivateLink? can Redwood run in our account or do we need cross-account endpoints?
00:02:18 Lena: two options — PrivateLink cross-account service endpoints (we host service endpoint in our VPC and you create an interface endpoint) or full-on customer-hosted deployment where Redwood control plane is private and runtime sits in your account. for compliance you probably want full customer runtime.
00:02:36 Hannah: is cross-account PrivateLink audited? we need flow logs and endpoint lifecycle controls.
00:02:41 Samir: we can provide full change history and flow logs; on PrivateLink we emit connection logs to your account via VPC flow logs and we can push our audit events to your S3 through a role.
00:02:52 Miguel: DNS — split-horizon: our internal resolver maps internal model artifact hostnames to internal storage. do you support custom resolvers on the worker nodes?
00:03:01 Lena: yes — in private deployment we configure the nodes to use your VPC DNS. important gotcha is NXDOMAIN or CNAME rewriting; the runtime retries on transient DNS failures and has a 200ms cold-start backoff. you can also provide an internal mirror of model artifacts to avoid egress.
00:03:18 Olivia (Dev): regarding caching: if the KV cache misses, how much latency are we adding?
00:03:24 Lena: depends on model and quantization; typical cold KV fetch (from S3/internal store) adds 10-40ms per request if it's a small key look; but if you proxy to a heavier store it could be 100-200ms. we recommend local SSD-backed KV with local replication for hot shards.
00:03:43 Priya: batching — our p95 latency target is 120ms, can you hit that with batching?
00:03:49 Jordan: yes if you tune batch size and priority queues. continuous batching with small max windows (e.g., 8-12ms) lets throughput be high while keeping p95 low. we aim to keep token-retention under 20ms per micro-batch when using quantized kernels.
00:04:07 Miguel: what about NUMA and CPU pinning? our infra team is sensitive to IRQ balancing.
00:04:12 Lena: runtime binds GPU workers to specific CPUs, we recommend isolating CPUs with cset or systemd CPUAffinity and using hugepages for memory-heavy models. pinning reduces kernel migrations and improves p95. we'll share recommended systemd unit examples.
00:04:28 Hannah: KMS/HSM — for key usage logs do you export key IDs or cleartext? we need key usage auditability without exposing plaintext.
00:04:36 Samir: we only log key IDs and operation metadata; plaintext never emitted. support for HSM-backed wrap/unwrap is available in private deployments.
00:04:45 Miguel: egress proxy — would you recommend hairpin NAT or an egress proxy for telemetry and updates?
00:04:51 Lena: hairpin NAT is simplest but conntrack increases and you hit state table. egress proxy (sidecar) gives more control (mTLS, routing, retries) and centralises TLS certs; tradeoff is additional hop and latency. for high-throughput low-latency we often push for an internal mirror + local artifact cache to avoid egress for model downloads.
00:05:10 Rajesh: quantization — 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs on hallucination and throughput?
00:05:15 Lena: 8-bit quant is lowest risk; 4-bit gives better throughput but can impact logits slightly. we do per-workload evals: Redwood Optimize can run a calibration suite and give an expected delta on accuracy vs throughput. choose 4-bit for bursty high-throughput non-critical tasks, 8-bit or float16 for critical clinical prompts.
00:05:35 Priya: runbook — if a shard loses KV cache, what's the failover?
00:05:40 Jordan: we have multi-replica hot shards; on fail we fallback to a nearby shard in same AZ then optionally to cold object store. there's also a degrade policy to lower batch depth and prefer single-token fetches to preserve latency SLO.
00:05:58 Miguel: can we see a config example for sharding and a failure injection plan?
00:06:03 Lena: yes we'll attach a sample 3-node shard config and a chaos test plan.
00:06:10 Hannah: slightly worried about DNS TTLs and cache poisoning in split-horizon — do you support DNS-over-TLS between worker and resolver?
00:06:17 Lena: yes we can enable DoT between nodes and your resolver. it's slightly heavier but recommended for security-sensitive setups.
00:06:25 Samir: quick demo idea — we can run a 2-hour lab where we spin up a pilot in your dev VPC, run a 50k qps egress-limited test and show latency/kv hit breakdown. would that help?
00:06:35 Priya: yes, but timeline — our security review must complete before we allow an external runner. we need the security docs and the PrivateLink attestation.
00:06:42 Samir: got it — we'll send the docs within 48 hours.
00:06:46 Rajesh: one more on batching — for streaming responses, does batching delay earliest tokens?
00:06:52 Jordan: streaming and batching interplay is tricky. we flush partial batches to emit first tokens early (head flushing) and then continue to batch the rest. it's a tunable parameter; you can set aggressive streaming latency targets and slightly sacrifice throughput.
00:07:10 Miguel: on conntrack — any recommendations to avoid NAT table exhaustion?
00:07:15 Lena: use connection pooling, reuse HTTP/2 multiplexing where possible, and prefer a sidecar proxy with keepalive. also increase conntrack table sizes and monitor ephemeral ports. we can share a prescriptive kernel sysctl list.
00:07:28 Priya: what metric dashboards will we get?
00:07:31 Samir: per-route latency breakdown (KV hit/miss, batch wait, model tokens), per-token cost, and per-shard cache hit rates. we'll show a demo dashboard in the pilot.
00:07:44 (Speaker 7): sorry, small noise here, cough.
00:07:50 Miguel: — so next, can you show us an example of the node bootstrap script and systemd units?
00:07:56 Lena: yes i'll include a sample. note we do driver pinning for GPUs, and we recommend using pinned interrupts for NICs on high-throughput boxes.
00:08:09 Hannah: on compliance: we need evidence of encryption in transit for inter-node KV replication.
00:08:14 Jordan: replication is TLS mTLS by default inside the cluster; we also support an optional VPN overlay if you prefer.
00:08:22 Priya: curious about cost tradeoffs: dedicated vs hosted — if we keep runtime inside our VPC, what are the main delta costs?
00:08:29 Samir: main differences: you bear infra and egress costs; Redwood charges a private deployment license + support. benefits are control, perf isolation, and compliance. we'll share a model to project unit token cost based on batch depth and cache hit rate.
00:08:45 Rajesh: can you run a benchmark with our histogram? like our request distribution is heavy-tailed.
00:08:51 Jordan: yes we can ingest your request trace (anonymized) and simulate in Redwood's scale lab. that's part of the pilot scope.
00:09:00 Miguel: regarding private artifacts mirror — how big would that be? we have 20 models, average 8GB each.
00:09:06 Lena: typical worker cache stores only the quantized weights per active model; if you want local mirror for all models you need tens to hundreds of GB per node. we recommend a central artifact store per AZ with SSD backed nodes and local LRU cache per worker.
